summary: This is a Makefile that defines a set of developer convenience commands for managing a Docusaurus blog project. Each command prints a yellow informational message to the terminal explaining what it does. The help target uses awk to parse and display all available commands in a formatted list, making it easy for developers to discover what they can do.

explanations.1: SHELL:=bash sets the shell interpreter that Make will use to execute commands to bash instead of the default sh.
explanations.3: COLOR_YELLOW:=33 defines a variable storing the ANSI color code for yellow (33), which will be reused in printf commands to colorize text output.
explanations.5: .PHONY: help tells Make that 'help' is not a real file but a command, so it should always run even if a file named 'help' exists.
explanations.8: The awk command parses the Makefile itself to find all targets with comments (marked by ##), extracts them, and formats them into a nice help menu with cyan-colored target names and descriptions.
explanations.13: printf with \e[1;${COLOR_YELLOW}m uses ANSI escape codes to print the message in bold yellow; \e[0m resets the formatting back to normal.
explanations.24: deploy: build means the deploy target depends on build—Make will run the build target first before running deploy.
